voice.refText: You wake up and discover you can pause time. 10 seconds once a day. At first, you use it for dumb things. You catch your falling coffee. You dodge your boss in the hallway.

lines.text: Ten o'clock. The doors open, and you've been holding this since four.
lines.say: [dry, close, a little breathless, no run-up] Ten o'clock. The doors open, and you've been holding this since four.

lines.text: What if you could see who wants you to fail?
lines.say: [curious, low, the question put plainly over the crimson card] What if you could see who wants you to fail?

lines.text: Because that's your best friend. And that's minus eighty-four.
lines.say: [quiet, flat, the second sentence slower and colder] Because that's your best friend. And that's minus eighty-four.

lines.text: Since this morning, a tag has opened over anyone who hears your good news. You've told no one all day.
lines.say: [warm, confiding, a touch amused at your restraint] Since this morning, a tag has opened over anyone who hears your good news. You've told no one all day.

lines.text: Not because of the tags. Because Min-jun hears everything first. He always has.
lines.say: [warm, fond, the last three words soft] Not because of the tags. Because Min-jun hears everything first. He always has.

lines.text: Min-jun: Knew it. Knew it.
lines.say: [delighted, loud, half a laugh, arm already round you] Knew it. Knew it.

lines.text: Sixty seconds. The card folds shut. His arm stays. So does the number.
lines.say: [dry, even, four short beats, the last one quiet] Sixty seconds. The card folds shut. His arm stays. So does the number.

lines.text: The rule, once. Say good news out loud, or what you're going for, to a face, and every time you say it a meter opens over whoever hears, for sixty seconds, from plus one hundred to minus one hundred.
lines.say: [exact, unhurried, laying it out once, a small lift on 'every time'] The rule, once. Say good news out loud, or what you're going for, to a face, and every time you say it a meter opens over whoever hears, for sixty seconds, from plus one hundred to minus one hundred.

lines.text: Plus one hundred: pure joy for you. Minus one hundred: they want you to fail.
lines.say: [level, the two halves weighed against each other, the last four words cold] Plus one hundred: pure joy for you. Minus one hundred: they want you to fail.

lines.text: It never says why. Calls, texts and posts open nothing. Remember that.
lines.say: [quiet, a warning, 'Remember that' slow and close] It never says why. Calls, texts and posts open nothing. Remember that.

lines.text: Every night, one kimbap, two halves. You take yours and watch him chew.
lines.say: [warm, amused, an ordinary ritual, the last word dry] Every night, one kimbap, two halves. You take yours and watch him chew.

lines.text: Your phone. Ji-yoon, your sister. Six years of nights at the depot to pay for that classroom. You tell her.
lines.say: [tender, a little proud of her, 'six years' slowed] Your phone. Ji-yoon, your sister. Six years of nights at the depot to pay for that classroom. You tell her.

lines.text: Ji-yoon: Say it again.
lines.say: Ji-yoon: Say it again.

lines.text: You do. You're grinning into a phone. Nothing opens over a phone. You still don't know her number.
lines.say: [warm, then the smile fading line by line, the last sentence quiet and exact] You do. You're grinning into a phone. Nothing opens over a phone. You still don't know her number.

lines.text: Next morning. You've worked it out. Crimson is for enemies. So you test it on one.
lines.say: [brisk, amused, confident the way you are, a glint on 'test'] Next morning. You've worked it out. Crimson is for enemies. So you test it on one.

lines.text: Tae-ho, at the shoe lockers. Trash-talks you every morning, two years running.
lines.say: [dry, a shrug in it] Tae-ho, at the shoe lockers. Trash-talks you every morning, two years running.

lines.text: Tae-ho: Still here?
lines.say: [bored, sneering, not looking up] Still here?

lines.text: You hold up the letter.
lines.say: [flat, a beat held, the card about to snap] You hold up the letter.

lines.text: Minus six. He barely looks up.
lines.say: [deflated, amused, the number almost a disappointment] Minus six. He barely looks up.

lines.text: Tae-ho: Nice. Move.
lines.say: [indifferent, already past you] Nice. Move.

lines.text: Ms. Kang.
lines.say: [a small lift, hopeful, two words] Ms. Kang.

lines.text: Ms. Kang: Good.
lines.say: [clipped, warm underneath, one word and back to the board] Good.

lines.text: That's all you get, and it's plus forty-one.
lines.say: [amused, warm, a little surprised by the number] That's all you get, and it's plus forty-one.

lines.text: The clerk at the store: zero. Grey. A tour group outside the station: eleven zeros. The cat on the crate: nothing. Cats don't count.
lines.say: [quick, deadpan, a list, the last three words thrown away] The clerk at the store: zero. Grey. A tour group outside the station: eleven zeros. The cat on the crate: nothing. Cats don't count.

lines.text: So the enemy doesn't care. Here's why.
lines.say: [curious, leaning in, the puzzle turning] So the enemy doesn't care. Here's why.

lines.text: We measure ourselves against people near our own level, not far above or below.
lines.say: [exact, calm, a finding stated once] We measure ourselves against people near our own level, not far above or below.

lines.text: And envy wants someone who started where you did, in a thing that matters to you.
lines.say: [low, closer, each clause landing nearer home] And envy wants someone who started where you did, in a thing that matters to you.

lines.text: Tae-ho has never once thought about you. Min-jun has the next desk, the same kimbap, the same four seats.
lines.say: [quiet, the second sentence slowing with each item, the last one almost hurt] Tae-ho has never once thought about you. Min-jun has the next desk, the same kimbap, the same four seats.

lines.text: But here's the problem. Problem one: the only people who can bleed at your news are the ones in your lane.
lines.say: [a turn, dry, the count stated plainly, the end heavy] But here's the problem. Problem one: the only people who can bleed at your news are the ones in your lane.

lines.text: So you ask him. Straight out, on the steps.
lines.say: [brisk, a decision made, a small breath before 'straight out'] So you ask him. Straight out, on the steps.

lines.text: He can't see it. Nobody sees the tags but you.
lines.say: [flat, gentle, a door closing] He can't see it. Nobody sees the tags but you.

lines.text: And people don't like to admit being maliciously envious, even to themselves.
lines.say: [quiet, exact, 'even to themselves' slowed] And people don't like to admit being maliciously envious, even to themselves.

lines.text: So you have a number. And no one to ask.
lines.say: [dry, resigned, two short sentences] So you have a number. And no one to ask.

lines.text: Eleven. Home. The letter's already on the fridge, next to the kimchi jar where her brushes have stood for six years.
lines.say: [hushed, warm, a tired house, the jar noticed and let go] Eleven. Home. The letter's already on the fridge, next to the kimchi jar where her brushes have stood for six years.

lines.text: She's in the doorway, pulling on the vest. She doesn't turn round.
lines.say: [soft, observed, the last sentence a half-beat late] She's in the doorway, pulling on the vest. She doesn't turn round.

lines.text: Ji-yoon: Say it again.
lines.say: Ji-yoon: Say it again.

lines.text: You say it to her back. Nothing opens. A back is not a face.
lines.say: [quiet, a rule remembered, the last sentence exact and a little rueful] You say it to her back. Nothing opens. A back is not a face.

lines.text: She laughs, and she's gone.
lines.say: [warm, light, over before it lands] She laughs, and she's gone.

lines.text: And she still hasn't seen your face say it. Not yet.
lines.say: [low, an open door, 'not yet' slow] And she still hasn't seen your face say it. Not yet.

lines.text: Minus six for the rival. So maybe the number fades the further someone is from your lane. One way to find out.
lines.say: [curious, scheming, a grin in the last five words] Minus six for the rival. So maybe the number fades the further someone is from your lane. One way to find out.

lines.text: Daechi-dong has about a thousand cram schools.
lines.say: [exact, matter-of-fact, setting a stage] Daechi-dong has about a thousand cram schools.

lines.text: Seoul lets them teach only between five in the morning and ten at night, and inspectors have patrolled the streets to make sure.
lines.say: [dry, a little wry on 'inspectors', even pace] Seoul lets them teach only between five in the morning and ten at night, and inspectors have patrolled the streets to make sure.

lines.text: So at ten, every door on the street opens at once.
lines.say: [a lift, the picture arriving, 'at once' bright] So at ten, every door on the street opens at once.

lines.text: You stand on the academy steps. And you say it. Into the crowd.
lines.say: [held breath, three beats, the last two words thrown out and let fall] You stand on the academy steps. And you say it. Into the crowd.

lines.text: A thousand strangers. A thousand zeros. A scatter of teal. And three crimson. All by the kimbap shop. All from your class.
lines.say: [awed, slow, counting the field, the last two sentences cold] A thousand strangers. A thousand zeros. A scatter of teal. And three crimson. All by the kimbap shop. All from your class.

lines.text: So. Minus means they want you to fail. And now you know exactly who to cut.
lines.say: [hard, decided, a wrong certainty, 'exactly' sharp] So. Minus means they want you to fail. And now you know exactly who to cut.

lines.text: Your year is the last one graded on the old school curve.
lines.say: [exact, a little ominous, plain] Your year is the last one graded on the old school curve.

lines.text: The top school grade goes to the top four per cent, and the five-tier scale after you widens it to ten per cent.
lines.say: [level, two facts set side by side, 'after you' pointed] The top school grade goes to the top four per cent, and the five-tier scale after you widens it to ten per cent.

lines.text: In your class, call it four seats. Min-jun wants one. So do you.
lines.say: [quiet, the arithmetic landing on two people, the last three words soft] In your class, call it four seats. Min-jun wants one. So do you.

lines.text: So the meter becomes a weapon.
lines.say: [cold, short, a turn] So the meter becomes a weapon.

lines.text: Each mock score, you stand up and say it out loud, and read the room.
lines.say: [brisk, clinical, 'read the room' almost a sneer] Each mock score, you stand up and say it out loud, and read the room.

lines.text: Anyone past minus forty goes out of the group chat.
lines.say: [flat, efficient, a rule being applied] Anyone past minus forty goes out of the group chat.

lines.text: Keep the past-paper file moving, or keep the seat? You keep the seat.
lines.say: [a choice put quickly, answered at once, no pride in it] Keep the past-paper file moving, or keep the seat? You keep the seat.

lines.text: And every night at the counter:
lines.say: [softer, the ritual returning, left hanging] And every night at the counter:

lines.text: You walk past it.
lines.say: [quiet, three words, a small ache under the flatness] You walk past it.

lines.text: You climb. Three mock scores. Three announcements.
lines.say: [clipped, rising, a count up] You climb. Three mock scores. Three announcements.

lines.text: But the higher you go, the redder the room.
lines.say: [low, the turn, 'redder' slow] But the higher you go, the redder the room.

lines.text: When someone close beats you at something central to who you are, the closer they are, the sharper it cuts.
lines.say: [exact, unhurried, a finding that hurts, the end quiet] When someone close beats you at something central to who you are, the closer they are, the sharper it cuts.

lines.text: And his number keeps going down.
lines.say: [hushed, an open loop, 'down' falling] And his number keeps going down.

lines.text: Your score reaches the top. Min-jun's chair beside you stays empty.
lines.say: [even, two pictures, the second one slower, nothing added] Your score reaches the top. Min-jun's chair beside you stays empty.

lines.text: The reading room. Past midnight. His seat's empty, and his notebook's open.
lines.say: [hushed, close, a lamp and a page] The reading room. Past midnight. His seat's empty, and his notebook's open.

lines.text: Your wrong answers, from the past papers you binned. Copied out in his hand. Beside each one, one word. Why.
lines.say: [slow, realising, each clause a step, the last word barely voiced] Your wrong answers, from the past papers you binned. Copied out in his hand. Beside each one, one word. Why.

lines.text: He isn't sawing your chair. He's climbing.
lines.say: [quiet, the floor shifting, the last two words warm] He isn't sawing your chair. He's climbing.

lines.text: Envy comes in two kinds: benign envy pushes you to move up, malicious envy to pull the other person down.
lines.say: [exact, calm, the two kinds held apart with the hands] Envy comes in two kinds: benign envy pushes you to move up, malicious envy to pull the other person down.

lines.text: So the store was wrong. Minus never meant they want you to fail. It meant it hurt.
lines.say: [low, the planted line taken back, the last three words slow and gentle] So the store was wrong. Minus never meant they want you to fail. It meant it hurt.

lines.text: In one brain-scan study, envying a peer who did better at something that mattered came with activity in a region also active in pain.
lines.say: [even, careful, 'one study' honest, the last word soft] In one brain-scan study, envying a peer who did better at something that mattered came with activity in a region also active in pain.

lines.text: A tag has one colour for every kind of hurt.
lines.say: [quiet, a complete thought, the landing line, no rush] A tag has one colour for every kind of hurt.

lines.text: But here's the second problem. Problem two: hurt needs a lane. Outside yours, nobody bleeds.
lines.say: [a turn, dry, the count plain, a certainty that will break] But here's the second problem. Problem two: hurt needs a lane. Outside yours, nobody bleeds.

lines.text: And you've only ever read one lane.
lines.say: [low, close, an open loop, 'one' pointed] And you've only ever read one lane.

lines.text: The school confirms it. Four years, paid. If the exam holds.
lines.say: [bright, then a catch on the last four words] The school confirms it. Four years, paid. If the exam holds.

lines.text: For once you run home instead of the store.
lines.say: [warm, quick, a little breathless, a small smile] For once you run home instead of the store.

lines.text: Ji-yoon's at the table. A night off. You say it to her face.
lines.say: [tender, the last sentence held a half-beat before the snap] Ji-yoon's at the table. A night off. You say it to her face.

lines.text: Both arms round you, and her face in your scarf.
lines.say: [soft, close, the picture only] Both arms round you, and her face in your scarf.

lines.text: Ji-yoon: Say it again.
lines.say: Ji-yoon: Say it again.

lines.text: Minus sixty-eight. Over the one person who ever asked to hear it twice.
lines.say: [flat, hollow, the number first, the rest slow] Minus sixty-eight. Over the one person who ever asked to hear it twice.

lines.text: You go stiff in the hug.
lines.say: [quiet, exact, five words, no comment] You go stiff in the hug.

lines.text: Ji-yoon: Say it again.
lines.say: Ji-yoon: Say it again.

lines.text: You can't.
lines.say: [barely voiced, two words] You can't.

lines.text: It's been measured. Couples whose partner meets good news with enthusiasm report more intimacy and satisfaction.
lines.say: [even, careful, a finding set beside the hug, not against it] It's been measured. Couples whose partner meets good news with enthusiasm report more intimacy and satisfaction.

lines.text: You just watched a tag say what her arms didn't.
lines.say: [low, hurt, 'didn't' falling] You just watched a tag say what her arms didn't.

lines.text: You take your bag. And you don't go home. Not that night. Not for a month.
lines.say: [flat, then each sentence longer and heavier, the last one quiet] You take your bag. And you don't go home. Not that night. Not for a month.

lines.text: A week at the reading room. You say nothing good out loud, to anyone, and the meters go quiet, because you have.
lines.say: [hushed, tired, the silence heard, 'because you have' gentle] A week at the reading room. You say nothing good out loud, to anyone, and the meters go quiet, because you have.

lines.text: Exam eve. Your mistake notebook, every error this year and why. Leave it, or keep the seat?
lines.say: [close, a choice put plainly, the question left in the air for half a beat] Exam eve. Your mistake notebook, every error this year and why. Leave it, or keep the seat?

lines.text: You leave it on his desk. Half a kimbap on top.
lines.say: [quiet, decided, a small warmth on the kimbap] You leave it on his desk. Half a kimbap on top.

lines.text: It might cost you a seat. You leave it anyway.
lines.say: [level, honest about the price, 'anyway' steady] It might cost you a seat. You leave it anyway.

lines.text: Exam day.
lines.say: [a breath, two words, the scale about to open] Exam day.

lines.text: Last year, the country grounded its flights for the English listening test. For thirty-five minutes, no plane crosses the sky while you listen.
lines.say: [awed, slow, the second sentence hushed, 'while you listen' close] Last year, the country grounded its flights for the English listening test. For thirty-five minutes, no plane crosses the sky while you listen.

lines.text: The market opens late. Police motorbikes carry the late ones to the gates. A country holds its breath for you.
lines.say: [even, wondering, the last sentence warm and slow] The market opens late. Police motorbikes carry the late ones to the gates. A country holds its breath for you.

lines.text: At your gate, in the crowd of parents: the warehouse vest. Straight off the shift. The lunch she packed.
lines.say: [hushed, a catch in it, three short pictures, the last one tender] At your gate, in the crowd of parents: the warehouse vest. Straight off the shift. The lunch she packed.

lines.text: You take the lunch. Neither of you says a word. Nothing opens.
lines.say: [quiet, still, the last two words almost relieved] You take the lunch. Neither of you says a word. Nothing opens.

lines.text: And results come in a month. For a month, you say nothing to anyone.
lines.say: [low, an open loop, 'nothing' slowed] And results come in a month. For a month, you say nothing to anyone.

lines.text: Results. Grade one. Grade one. Grade one. The scholarship holds.
lines.say: [tight, then three beats like flaps turning, then a breath out] Results. Grade one. Grade one. Grade one. The scholarship holds.

lines.text: Min-jun, beside you: grade one in maths too.
lines.say: [warm, surprised, glad for him] Min-jun, beside you: grade one in maths too.

lines.text: Out there the curve is the whole country's: in most subjects, the top four per cent of everyone who sat it.
lines.say: [exact, the picture widening, 'everyone' lifted] Out there the curve is the whole country's: in most subjects, the top four per cent of everyone who sat it.

lines.text: The same four per cent. A seat in one case, and a sea in the other.
lines.say: [quiet, a mirror turning, the two words set against each other] The same four per cent. A seat in one case, and a sea in the other.

lines.text: You gave him the notebook thinking it was your seat. It was never a seat.
lines.say: [soft, rueful, the second sentence slow] You gave him the notebook thinking it was your seat. It was never a seat.

lines.text: You take it.
lines.say: [warm, three words, a small smile] You take it.

lines.text: Now her. Text her, and never see her colour again. Or take the bus to the depot and say it to her face.
lines.say: [the dilemma, put plainly, both halves given their weight, no steer] Now her. Text her, and never see her colour again. Or take the bus to the depot and say it to her face.

lines.text: A text would open nothing. You could keep her forever on a screen.
lines.say: [low, tempting, honest, 'forever' slow] A text would open nothing. You could keep her forever on a screen.

lines.text: You're on the bus.
lines.say: [flat, decided, four words, a breath after] You're on the bus.

lines.text: Across eleven studies, the most common regret of a life is education, about a third of all regrets.
lines.say: [even, quiet, a fact laid down gently on the bus seat beside you] Across eleven studies, the most common regret of a life is education, about a third of all regrets.

lines.text: Her brushes have stood in a jar for six years.
lines.say: [hushed, the fact landing on her, 'six years' slow] Her brushes have stood in a jar for six years.

lines.text: Six o'clock. Her shift ends. You stand on the dock. And you say it.
lines.say: [held, close, four beats, the last one let go] Six o'clock. Her shift ends. You stand on the dock. And you say it.

lines.text: The same.
lines.say: [flat, two words, no surprise left] The same.

lines.text: She holds on. And this time you don't go stiff.
lines.say: [warm, quiet, 'this time' gentle] She holds on. And this time you don't go stiff.

lines.text: Ji-yoon: Say it again.
lines.say: [first, down the phone: bright, laughing, hungry for it; second, in the doorway with her back to you: thrown over a shoulder, easy, half a yawn; third, through the hug: wet, muffled in your scarf, joyful; fourth, into your shoulder, a moment later: smaller, pleading; fifth, on the dock: steady, crying, asking for it the way she always has] Say it again.

lines.text: You say it again. The flaps fold at sixty seconds. And snap open.
lines.say: [steady, then the clock, then the snap, the last three words hushed] You say it again. The flaps fold at sixty seconds. And snap open.

lines.text: You said nobody outside your lane bleeds.
lines.say: [low, after the silence, the old line read back to you] You said nobody outside your lane bleeds.

lines.text: She was never outside your lane. She was in it first.
lines.say: [quiet, exact, the turn, 'first' soft and complete] She was never outside your lane. She was in it first.

lines.text: Six years ago it was her letter on the fridge.
lines.say: [hushed, a picture from before you, slow] Six years ago it was her letter on the fridge.

lines.text: At the 1992 Olympics, bronze medallists looked happier than silver. Silver thinks of the gold it nearly won. Bronze thinks of nearly winning nothing.
lines.say: [even, warm, a finding told like a story, the two sentences weighed against each other] At the nineteen ninety-two Olympics, bronze medallists looked happier than silver. Silver thinks of the gold it nearly won. Bronze thinks of nearly winning nothing.

lines.text: She's not watching you fail. She's watching the life she handed you walk up the dock with the news. And she wants it in.
lines.say: [tender, slow, the second sentence a long picture, the last four words simple] She's not watching you fail. She's watching the life she handed you walk up the dock with the news. And she wants it in.

lines.text: The same number. The same arms. You hold on through the second sixty.
lines.say: [quiet, two beats and a complete thought, 'hold on' steady] The same number. The same arms. You hold on through the second sixty.

lines.text: Morning. The fridge. She unpins the calendar, and behind it is a letter. Hers. Six years old.
lines.say: [hushed, morning light, the reveal in two small words] Morning. The fridge. She unpins the calendar, and behind it is a letter. Hers. Six years old.

lines.text: She tapes yours beside it. She doesn't ask. You don't say it. And you don't pull back.
lines.say: [warm, even, four short facts, the last one gentle] She tapes yours beside it. She doesn't ask. You don't say it. And you don't pull back.

lines.text: The brushes stay in the jar.
lines.say: [quiet, six words, left as they are] The brushes stay in the jar.

lines.text: Tomorrow someone you love will pause half a second before they say congratulations.
lines.say: [close, warm, speaking to the viewer now, 'half a second' slowed] Tomorrow someone you love will pause half a second before they say congratulations.

lines.text: That half-second is the other life, going past.
lines.say: [quiet, a complete thought, the residue, no rush, 'going past' let go] That half-second is the other life, going past.

lines.text: Then the door. Min-jun. A letter of his own. He says it.
lines.say: [light, warm, then a catch on the last three words] Then the door. Min-jun. A letter of his own. He says it.

lines.text: So, would you still say it to her face? Tell us in the comments. And if you'd have done the same, hit like and subscribe.
lines.say: [warm, direct, the question real, the rest easy] So, would you still say it to her face? Tell us in the comments. And if you'd have done the same, hit like and subscribe.
